_comment: A voice constitution, specified where voice actually lives: syntax and cadence, not adjectives.
Prose style sheets say 'lucid, precise, unshowy' and four books obey that and come out identical.
This file is the half a style sheet cannot express. Copy it to <book>/editorial/voice-profile.json,
set the targets, then: python3 desk/tools/prose_audit.py <book>/manuscript --profile <that file>
See desk/method/07-voice-engineering.md for how to choose the numbers, and
desk/method/06-idiolect-ledger.md for what the inherited bans are and why they are cumulative.

cadence._comment: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — never hand these to a drafting agent as a target. Tested: given numeric cadence targets, drafts came back rated 3.0/10 quality and 8.7/10 mannered, last of six by every judge ('you can hear the period key being pressed'). See method/07-voice-engineering.md. Use them to DETECT drift back to the median-11 default, then fix by rewriting the prose brief, not by asking for shorter sentences.

_comment: Instances per 10,000 words. Ceilings, not targets. These are the constraints that WORK: a prohibition
leaves the solution unspecified, so it must be invented; a target names it, so it can be complied with.
Rule R-voice: bans name a CONSTRUCTION, never a phrase. Sentience banned 'I want to be precise about'
and got 'true / clear / modest / careful' instead. Run the measure/revise loop against THESE (it is the
only thing that reaches zero) and never against the cadence block above.

declared_refrains: _comment: phrases the style sheet deliberately repeats. The audit stops calling these refrains.
_comment: everything NOT listed here that recurs in 3+ chapters is self-priming, not craft.
_comment: each declared refrain must name its owner and its home chapter in the style sheet.

_comment: Per-narrator fingerprints, assigned BEFORE drafting and audited after (R15).
Parallel drafting agents diverge on facts and converge on tics. The ledger defends the facts;
this defends the voices. Give each narrator a syntactic habit, a metaphor domain it owns
exclusively, a characteristic evasion, and one figure no other narrator may touch.

NARRATOR_A.syntax: long subordinated sentences that qualify themselves; rarely a fragment
owns_figures: the specific image only this narrator may use
NARRATOR_A.evasion: what this narrator reaches for instead of saying the true thing

NARRATOR_B.syntax: parataxis; short declaratives joined by 'and'; fragments permitted

screen._comment: The aridity screen (method/05). abstract_terms are THIS book's idea vocabulary; people are the characters whose presence anchors a scene. Both are book-specific — declare them or the screen is skipped.

forbidden_image_bank._comment: The most productive constraint in testing: forbid a whole metaphorical domain so the book's central conceits must be reinvented rather than retrieved. Name the domain this book OWNS and the domain it may not enter.
